g: Grilling round 1 (2026-10-14): what to design next, and glossary words that are wrong or missing

ctx: You didn't name a topic. These are the open design areas that don't depend on art.
o: Kingdom Overview and Goods strip: the HUD parts the design asks for but the game never built (sortable Town table, kingdom-wide Goods with prices and trends, the Resource Flow overlay, alert icons over Towns; K opens the Castle today, not an overview)
Balance and run length: back-haul made Victory faster (163 game-minutes in the scripted run; your target is about 4 hours)
Only the glossary questions below, then stop

q: The glossary says a Trader travels "by road", but roads are optional (off-road is half speed). Change it to "by road or across open ground"?

The glossary says the Castle is "at the board's origin", but the game puts it at a seeded spot, off-centre, at least 2 hexes from the edge. Change it to "at a seeded spot on the board where every realm starts"?

A Trader going out to buy now also carries its home Town's surplus and sells it to the Town it visits. What do we call that? (Players never see the word; it's for the design docs and for talking to me.)
o: Back-haul (the usual logistics word; the design doc already uses it)

q: Each sale makes a Town ask a little more for that Good (up to 1.35×); unsold Goods slowly get cheaper (down to 0.75×). What do we call that?
Should players see it? For example "Potato asking price +15%" in the Town panel's Stock list.
o: Yes, in the Town panel's Stock list, so players see why a Town's prices climb

q: A Town's own gold has no glossary word yet. Add Purse: "a Town's own gold; it has a limit set by the Town's level; anything above the limit is spent by the residents". Treasury stays the Crown's gold, and Budget is avoided.
o: Yes: Purse for a Town, Treasury for the Crown, never mixed

q: Three more words used in the game have no glossary entry: Royal Trader (the Castle's own Trader, buying research materials for the Castle Stock), Give and Take (the Crown moving 1,000 gold into or out of a Town's Purse; Take is a safety net, not income). Add all three, and avoid calling Take "Tax" or "Levy" (Tax already means what residents pay)?
o: Yes, add all three; Take: avoid Tax and Levy
